plain_claim: In the running signature S₀, the default printer (which elides numeral types, type arguments and coercions) maps the distinct closed terms (2 : Nat) - 3 = 0 and (2 : Int) - 3 = 0 to the same text 2 - 3 = 0; the first is valid and the second is not; and for every reader R (any function from a signature and a text to an optional term), R does not return (2 : Nat) - 3 = 0 on the default text of the first, or R does not return (2 : Int) - 3 = 0 on the default text of the second.
nonvacuity_witness: No hypotheses: the statement is about two concrete closed terms of S₀.
non_claims: Does not say that default text is usually ambiguous: one collision is exhibited; how often collisions occur in any real corpus is not examined.

Does not say that every reader misreads 2 - 3 = 0: the system elaborator reads it as the Nat statement (default_and_min_texts_faithful_for_cfg0_but_not_other_readers); the impossibility is that no single reader returns both terms.
Escape hatch: a printer that shows an annotation separating the two terms defeats the impossibility (positive control ppExplicit_separates_natSub_intSub).

Does not formalize Pollack-inconsistency: the toy has no proof system, so the collision is a toy analogue of one Pollack-axiom in the sense of Wiedijk (2012, Definition 1.4), not a derivation of a contradiction (Definition 1.5).

Text in this package is a parsed syntax tree (Stx), not a character string. That Lean v4.34.1 prints both statements as 2 - 3 = 0 by default is a separate build-checked observation (LeanObservations.lean), not a consequence of this theorem.

plain_claim: For every configuration cfg, signature S and term t: if t is well typed in S, then cfg reads the deletion-greedy rendering ppMin cfg S t back as t.
definitions: ppMin cfg S t shows exactly the annotation positions kept by minMask cfg S t, the deletion-greedy selection: start from all annotation positions of t (the explicit text), visit them in pre-order, and drop a position whenever cfg still reads the rendering without it back as t. The name abbreviates 'locally minimal'; it is not a minimum-size printer.

hypotheses.name: ht : WellTyped S t
hypotheses.purpose: The deletion search starts from the explicit text, which is proved faithful for well-typed terms (explicit_printer_section_law); without well-typedness the greedy rendering need not be faithful (see the counterexample).
hypotheses.witness_class: an ill-typed variable term under cfg0

nonvacuity_witness: tTrunc is well typed and its default text is not faithful under cfg0, so ppMin must keep annotations.
non_claims: Guaranteed faithful for the reader cfg it was computed against; it neither establishes nor refutes faithfulness for other configurations, which can fail (default_and_min_texts_faithful_for_cfg0_but_not_other_readers: ppMin cfg0 S₀ tZ is the default text a - b = z, which cfgLeaves reads as a different term) or still hold (ppMin_cfg0_tEqAB_faithful_for_all_cfg: ppMin cfg0 S₀ tEqAB is faithful for every configuration, and ppMin cfg0 S₀ tTrunc is faithful for cfgIntNumerals).
Not a minimum-size rendering: ppMin_not_globally_minimal_cfg0 (under cfg0, 2 annotations kept where a faithful 1-annotation rendering exists) and ppMin_not_globally_minimal_on_tTrunc_cfgLeaves.
The kept set depends on the visiting order (visiting_order_changes_kept_set_on_tTrunc).
The rendering may read oddly to a human: for tTrunc under cfg0 it is a - b = a - ↑b.

Annotation tokens on the running examples (default / ppMin cfg0 / explicit): tTrunc 0/1/6, tZ 0/0/3, tIntSub 0/1/5, tNatSub 0/0/5 (annCount_overhead_examples); ppMin cfgLeaves: 2, 1, 1, 0 and ppMin cfgIntNumerals: 1, 0, 0, 1 (annCount_overhead_examples_other_readers).

ppMin models a search over annotation subsets checked by re-elaboration; it does not model Lean's pp.analyze, which is heuristic and does not add a numeral type to (2 : Int) - 3 = 0 (LeanObservations.lean).
